question: Why feed probabilities into a stacking model?
quick: Probabilities preserve uncertainty that hard class votes discard.
standard:
Probabilities preserve uncertainty that hard class votes discard.

soft_features flattens model-by-class probability vectors into per-sample features. hard_features one-hot encodes argmax predictions. enhanced_features adds confidence, entropy and pairwise agreement. The module provides several learned combiners and voting baselines.

For example, two classifiers can predict the same class with probabilities 0.51 and 0.99. A hard vote treats them equally, while probability features preserve that difference. A learned combiner can use patterns of confidence and disagreement to decide when to trust each model. Enhanced features add summaries of those patterns rather than only the class scores.

The danger is training the combiner on overly optimistic predictions from models evaluated on their own training examples. It can learn relationships that disappear on new data, producing an apparently strong but misleading ensemble.

Train combiners on predictions from held-out or out-of-fold data, never on in-sample base-model predictions. Validate probability shape, finite values and row sums. A powerful meta-model can otherwise learn training artifacts and appear better without generalizing.

Out-of-fold predictions solve the meta-training data problem by generating each training row's base predictions from models that did not fit that row. The final base models can then be refit according to a defined procedure. I would compare the learned combiner with mean probabilities and simple voting to establish whether the additional parameters justify their complexity.
mistake: Training and evaluating a combiner on leaked predictions.

question: How does TreeStack convert model predictions into ensemble features?
quick: soft_features flattens model-by-class probability vectors into per-sample features. hard_features one-hot encodes argmax predictions. enhanced_features adds confidence, entropy and pairwise agreement. The module provides several learned combiners and voting baselines.
standard:
soft_features flattens model-by-class probability vectors into per-sample features. hard_features one-hot encodes argmax predictions. enhanced_features adds confidence, entropy and pairwise agreement. The module provides several learned combiners and voting baselines.

I would follow the prediction tensor into the feature builder. Soft features retain each model's probability for every class; hard features convert each model's top class into a one-hot vector. Enhanced features add summaries such as confidence, entropy, and agreement. The output must preserve sample order and class alignment before entering a combiner.

A tiny two-model, two-class example is enough to show how the flattened columns are constructed and why probabilities contain more information than class labels.

question: How would you test and improve TreeStack CNN?
quick: I would establish a reproducible baseline and test the specific failure boundary exposed by this implementation.
standard:
I would establish a reproducible baseline and test the specific failure boundary exposed by this implementation.

Train combiners on predictions from held-out or out-of-fold data, never on in-sample base-model predictions. Validate probability shape, finite values and row sums. A powerful meta-model can otherwise learn training artifacts and appear better without generalizing.

The first test boundary is data leakage: every meta-training prediction must come from a base model that did not train on that example. The second is feature correctness: shapes, class columns, and uncertainty calculations must match the intended representation. The third is actual benefit compared with simple fusion.

I would compare hard voting, probability averaging, and learned combiners on the same held-out data. This prevents a more expressive method from receiving credit merely because it had a more favorable split.

Keep the current implementation separate from the proposed improvement. Save representative inputs, expected outputs and a versioned configuration. Test normal inputs, malformed inputs and the failure case described above. For model outputs, include a held-out evaluation and inspect errors rather than treating a confidence field as proof.
